blocks.text: 04-BRD / brand Goes here. The end-to-end framework for designing a brand's visual identity from scratch. Covers brand strategy (mission, vision, core values), establishing creative directions via mood boards, semiotic sketching, and finalizing visual assets (typography, color palettes, and textures) for physical packaging. Not here. • Defining the specific psychographics of the target consumer -> 02-AVT • Managing freelance client contracts and invoicing platforms -> 21-OPS • Supply chain logistics for physical product packaging -> 18-COG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the step-by-step process of translating abstract brand strategy and core values into a tangible visual identity, emphasizing the use of semiotics and mood boards to prevent scope creep. modules: [BRD] topics: [brand strategy, creative direction, logo design, visual identity, semiotics] tier: 2 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. brand strategy / defining purpose, mission, and non-negotiable core values (e.g., ethical farming, sustainability, regional pride) to serve as creative filters; visual identity / building mood boards (compiling references from Pinterest, Behance, Cosmos) to establish creative directions and set client expectations early; semiotics / the sketching phase, intentionally avoiding category cliches (e.g., rejecting mountains/pine trees for a Himalayan brand) and analyzing symbol associations (rejecting a clover leaf for being too Irish, selecting a ginkgo leaf for Asian associations of longevity and peace); asset creation / vectorizing the logo, pairing it with editorial serif typography, and establishing a minimal color palette (black, white, red accents) enhanced by organic paper textures.

The 3-Direction Mood Board Framework: Presenting distinct visual routes (e.g., 1. Fun/vibrant, 2. Editorial/clean, 3. Minimal/vintage Asian stamps) to lock in the aesthetic early and avoid unnecessary revisions.
Semiotic Filtering: The explicit process of exploring symbols and rejecting them based on cultural mismatch, leading to the selection of the ginkgo leaf encapsulated in a traditional seal format.

Brand Alignment Definition: The principle that core values are not just formalities, but "creative filters for every decision that comes next," ensuring design is rooted in alignment rather than just aesthetics.
Skip. Promotional pitches for freelance platforms (Contra.com), invoicing, or managing international payments.
Scope mix. 100% baseline (the foundational process of building a visual brand identity). Volume. ~350 words.

02-AVT / avatars and jobs to be done Goes here. Identifying the target audience and aligning the brand's core values to consumer psychographics. Not here. • Designing the visual logo and color palette to appeal to this audience -> 04-BRD

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Highlights how defining the target audience's psychographics and values serves as the foundational filter for all subsequent creative and strategic decisions. modules: [AVT] topics: [audience identification, psychographics, brand alignment] tier: 2 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. psychographics / identifying "modern conscious consumers" who value food curiosity, experimentation, authenticity, and the story behind the product; alignment / establishing core values that mirror the target audience's worldview.
Audience Profiling: Moving beyond demographics to target consumers based on their curiosity, desire for experimentation, and appreciation for authenticity and regional story.
Skip. The visual design elements, logo sketches, or product packaging details.
